Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Voltara Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Marcus Hale, CEO; Sarah Chen, CFO; Tom Reilly, Chief Manufacturing Officer; Dr. Lena Novak, Chief Technology Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Marcus Hale.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 2024 was a transformative quarter for Voltara Motors, underscoring our leadership in the premium EV segment amid a rapidly evolving global market. We delivered record revenue of $6.7 billion, up 27% year-over-year and 12% quarter-over-quarter, surpassing our guidance and analyst expectations. This marked our ninth straight quarter of accelerating growth, driven by a 27% surge in vehicle deliveries to 128,450 units—our highest ever—fueled by ramps at Gigafactory Nevada and strong demand for our Apex SUV and Titan platforms.

Gross profit hit $1.64 billion, with segment-adjusted gross margins at 24.5%, expanding 420 basis points year-over-year thanks to cost discipline, scale, and vertical integration. Adjusted EBITDA reached $850 million, up 95% YoY at a 12.7% margin. We generated $750 million in operating cash flow, pushing unrestricted liquidity to $12 billion for our growth agenda.

Key wins included 14.2% U.S. premium EV market share, up from 9.8%, per Cox data, via IRA incentives and our "EV Everywhere" program. Globally, we grew to 3.4% share in top markets. Vehicle margins hit 25.1% on 22% lower battery costs from in-house LFP-NMC packs. Energy services added $280 million recurring revenue, up 110% YoY.

Innovation shone with OTA 4.2.1 rollout to 95% of fleet, boosting efficiency 15% and Level 3+ autonomy. Solid-state pilots produced 5,000 packs at 450 Wh/kg. Sustainability: 92% recycled battery content, 28% emissions cut, earning Dow Jones Sustainability Index nod.

North America drove 72% revenue, Europe 18%, APAC 8%. Gigafactory Texas hit 1,200 vehicles/day. We closed $1.2B VoltCore acquisition for solid-state acceleration, launched robotaxi pilots generating $20M MaaS revenue.

Q4 guide: $7.2-7.5B revenue, 140-150K deliveries, 25-26% margins. FY24: $25B revenue, 550K deliveries. 2025: 800K+ units, $40B revenue, FCF positive. This validates our "Scale Smart, Charge Ahead" strategy as EV adoption hits 18% U.S., 22% Europe.

We achieved notable milestones in total vehicle deliveries volume, capital expenditure plans, ASP trends, production ramps, charging network growth, and overall performance. We're particularly pleased with the initial customer response to our Voltara Spark hatchback, and its early traction in the sub-$30K segment is building a substantial backlog.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Marcus. Good morning, everyone. For Q3 2024, our revenue reached $6.7 billion, demonstrating a 27% increase compared to the same period last year. Our gross margin stood at 24.5%, reflecting our commitment to operational excellence. Operating expenses amounted to $1.2 billion, and net income was $450 million. We maintain a robust financial position with $12 billion in cash and cash equivalents. Our outlook for Q4 is revenue of $7.2 to $7.5 billion, with deliveries of 140,000 to 150,000 units.

I'll now dive into our core operational metric: total vehicle deliveries volume, which came in at 128,450 units for the quarter ended September 30, 2024. This represents a robust 27% year-over-year increase from 101,200 units in Q3 2023, and a solid 8% sequential growth from 118,900 units in Q2 2024. These figures underscore our accelerating production ramp at Gigafactory Nevada and the strong market reception of our refreshed lineup amid a competitive EV landscape.

Breaking this down by model: Our flagship Voltara Apex SUV, our volume leader with its 500+ mile EPA range on our proprietary LFP-NMC hybrid battery pack, delivered 72,300 units—up 32% YoY. This was driven by the mid-quarter launch of the Apex Long Range Plus variant, featuring our next-gen 800V architecture for 10-80% charging in under 18 minutes, which accounted for 45% of Apex deliveries. Demand outpaced supply, with U.S. wait times extending to 12 weeks.

The Voltara Titan pickup, our heavy-duty EV truck competing with Ford's F-150 Lightning and Rivian's R1T, hit 38,200 units—a stellar 42% YoY surge. Key tailwinds included bidirectional charging (V2G/V2L) capabilities, certified to UL 2594 standards, and a $7,500 federal IRA tax credit boosting fleet orders from UPS and FedEx. We saw strong uptake in our MegaPack option, adding 200 kWh of tow-rated capacity.

The Voltara Pulse sedan delivered 15,500 units, flat YoY as we deprioritize sedans for high-margin SUVs and trucks, while the new Voltara Spark hatchback notched 2,450 units in its first full quarter—early success in the sub-$30K segment against the Chevy Bolt EUV.

Regionally, North America was 62% of total at 79,640 units, up 35% YoY, on IRA-compliant content over 60% and incentives in California and Texas. Europe was 22% or 28,260 units, up 15% YoY despite German subsidy cuts; Berlin-assembled Apex captured 2.1% premium SUV share, edging Audi Q8 e-tron. China 12% or 15,410 units, down 5% YoY on BYD/Xiaomi pressure, but Shanghai JV with CATL improved COGS 12% via localized 4680 cells. Emerging markets added 4% or 5,140 units, with Australia RHD Titans gaining traction.

Delivery mix shifted to higher-ASP models, SUVs/trucks at 85% vs. 78% last year, supporting Q3 ASP of $52,300—up 4% YoY. Inventory ended lean at 18,000 units globally, down from 25,000 in Q2. Production utilization hit 92% record, with 85 GWh battery capacity secured from Panasonic and LG, insulating from 2023 shortages.

These results track to 550,000 FY2024 deliveries, 30%+ growth as #4 U.S. EV maker. Enablers: FSD Beta v12.5 to 40% fleet via OTA, 25% retention lift; $450M regulatory credits. Q4 guide 140-150K units on Titan doubling and Spark ramp. Risks: U.S. policy shifts, China tariffs, but 40% margin trajectory offers flexibility.

As we navigate moderating global EV sales growth—up 25% YoY through Q3—our capital allocation focuses on long-term leadership in affordable, high-margin EVs. For FY2024, we're at the high end of $5.2-5.5 billion CapEx, $4.1B YTD up 15% YoY into scaling and localization. FY2025 CapEx raised to $7.8B, up 45%, and $8.5-9.0B FY2026, per "Scale Smart" amid softening ASPs.

FY2025 allocation: Manufacturing 45% or $3.5B—ramping to 1.2M units YE2025 from 850K 2024. $1.8B Gigafactory Nevada Phase 2 for 100 GWh 4680 dry electrode by mid-2026, 20% cost cut. $800M Berlin to 300K units/year for Spark successor, qualifying EU credits and ZEV mandate. NA 55% for IRA $7,500/$35/kWh credits.

Battery/supply chain 30% or $2.3B: LFP now 60% mix at $85/kWh; $1.2B sodium-ion pilots Shanghai CATL for 15% savings by 2027, dodging cobalt volatility. $700M SC cathode with Umicore for 100% NA materials, IRA compliance, cutting China exposure to 25% YE2026.

Autonomy/software 15% or $1.2B: $600M Voltara NeuralNet on 5B fleet miles, NVIDIA OrinX for 2026 Pulse refresh. $400M digital twins for 30% faster changeovers.

Charging/other 10% or $800M: $500M for 5,000 DC fast chargers on US highways (IRA NEVI 40%) and German Autobahns; rest power electronics, 95% recycling by 2028.

Investments yield 25%+ 3-year IRR, 18% margins on LFP vs. 12% legacy. Prioritize US/EU 75%; India MoU $500M for 10% volume 2027. Payback 2.5 years, ROIC to 22% FY2027. Flex 10-15% if demand softens, $12B liquidity aids.

Before questions, a deep dive into ASP trends by model and region. ASP reflects mix, incentives, configurator uptake, pricing power vs. Tesla/BYD/VW. Q3 blended ASP $52,300, up 1.8% YoY from $51,400, flat seq. Pricing discipline: +3% retail ex-fleet. Battery costs down 12% YoY to <$110/kWh, 28% non-GAAP auto margins despite leasing.

By model: Pulse sedan (~25% volume) ASP $41,200 up 4.2% YoY; base 60 at $38,500, Long Range 80 $44,800 62% mix on FSD bundles +$1,200. Apex SUV (~55%) $56,700 up 5.1%; 100 $54,200, Performance $62,400 28% mix on CTP packs -18% BoM, 32% margins on 4680. Titan (~20%) $78,500 on 85% Tri-Motor take rate, $72,900 base, outperforming Cybertruck via steer-by-wire.

Regions: NA 52% rev ASP $58,200 +6% YoY, premium mix IRA tailwinds, retail $61,400. Europe 22% $47,800 flat, subsidy volatility offset Norway exemptions. China 18% $38,900 -3%, BYD pressure but Colossus pre-orders $76k. RoW 8% $49,200 +4%, APAC Apex strength.

Outlook: Q4 $52,500-53,500, 2-3% growth; premium shift 55%, FSD 42% attach.

Next, I'll hand to Tom for manufacturing update.

Tom Reilly:
Thank you, Sarah. Our manufacturing facilities are operating at peak efficiency to meet growing demand. Fremont Gigafactory equivalent in Nevada at 96.8% utilization, Texas at 91.4%, Monterrey at 78.5%. We've implemented lean principles, AI robotics cutting defects 35%, cycle times under 9 hours.

In Q3, record production of 135,000 vehicles, up 28% YoY from 105,000, 12% seq from Q2 120,000—tracking FY 550K. Deliveries trailed slightly at 128K on logistics.

Model mix: Apex SUV 55% or 74,000 units up 32% on LFP/CATL. Pulse sedan 28% 38,000, Titan 17% 23,000 up 150% on 4680 clearing constraints.

Overall utilization 93.2%, above 75% OEM avg. NA 68% production, Europe 22%, APAC 10%. Supply resilience: 95% raw mats locked, digital twins 98% OEE, 25% margin expansion. Workforce +4,200, 3.2% attrition.

Q4 145K+ at 94-96%. Long-term $12B capex India Giga 2026, 3M run-rate. Production is our edge—lower costs, faster FSD iteration.

Following Tom, Dr. Novak on tech advancements.

Dr. Lena Novak:
Thank you. We invest heavily in R&D for EV leadership. Advancements in battery tech—LFP-NMC hybrids, 4680, sodium-ion pilots—and autonomy position us strongly.

On charging: Our Voltara Charge Network (VCN) has 52,000 stalls at 8,200+ sites, +28% YoY, 12% seq; 4,200 new Q3, $1.2B YTD capex to $4.5B FY. 65% 350kW+ V4 DC, NACS/CCS compatible.

Utilization 32.4% avg daily, +450bps QoQ +18% YoY >25% industry. Peak 58%, off-peak 22% on dynamic pricing. V4 41%, 1.2M kWh/stall TTM. L2 18%. Revenue $285M Q3 +62% YoY, $1,450/stall, 68% margins on lower power costs.

NA 72% stalls 35% util, NEVI $450M grants, 85% NACS. Europe 18% 28% util, IONITY/AFIR. APAC 10% 26%, China 39%.

VCN Edge AI cuts queues 37%, throughput +22%; liquid-cooled cables. V2X pilots 12% rev. 92% loyalty, $0.14/kWh cost. Q4 34-36% util, 5K stalls. $1.2B ann rev machine.

We're on the forefront with NeuralNet on 5B miles, OTA FSD v12.5, solid-state 450 Wh/kg.

Now, I'll hand back to the operator for Q&A.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star one. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks. Marcus, great deliveries beat. Can you expand on the mix shift to higher ASP models and any pricing actions planned for Q4 amid competition?

Marcus Hale:
Thanks, John. Yes, SUVs and trucks hit 85% mix, driving the 4% ASP uplift to $52,300. We're holding discipline—no broad cuts—with dynamic configurators and FSD bundles adding $1,200 ASP. Q4 actions limited to targeted fleet promos; IRA keeps us competitive.

Operator:
Next from Emily Chen, Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Sarah, on CapEx acceleration to $7.8B FY25—how does that reconcile with softening demand signals, and ROIC trajectory?

Sarah Chen:
Emily, solid question. Acceleration targets high-ROI: Nevada Phase 2 25%+ IRR, payback 2.5 years. Demand softens but we're prioritizing LFP platforms at 18% margins. ROIC expands to 22% FY27 from 16%, flex down 10-15% if needed with $12B liquidity.

Operator:
From Mike Torres, Barclays.

Analyst 3:
Tom, impressive 93% utilization. Details on Texas Titan line and Mexico ramp risks?

Tom Reilly:
Mike, Texas Phase 2 structural packs eliminate 70 welds, full rate now. Monterrey at 78.5% scales to 90% Q4 with local 80% content dodging tariffs. Risks mitigated by cross-training, 98% tier-1 delivery.

Operator:
From Lisa Grant, JPMorgan.

Analyst 4:
Lena, charging utilization up nicely. V2G monetization timeline and third-party revenue share?

Dr. Lena Novak:
Lisa, V2G pilots yield 12% ancillary rev now, full H1 2025. Third-party 30% of rev, up on NACS; loyalty 92% from ecosystem ties. Positions VCN for 70%+ margins 2026.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for two more.

Operator:
From David Lee, RBC.

Analyst 5:
Marcus, regional highlights—China down YoY, any JV updates?

Marcus Hale:
David, China 12% deliveries but COGS -12% via CATL 4680 localization. Shanghai JV ramps Q4, countering BYD pricing; focus share first.

Operator:
Last from Anna Patel, Deutsche Bank.

Analyst 6:
Sarah, overall FY24 guide intact post-Q3? Margin drivers?

Sarah Chen:
Anna, yes—550K deliveries, $25B rev. Margins to 25%+ on cell costs -22%, localization 85% U.S., credits $450M. FSD retention +25%.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Marcus Hale for closing remarks.

Marcus Hale:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and remain committed to creating long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to sharing our progress with you next quarter.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the Voltara Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
